findings.title: Clearing skills at an agent switch still lets the old list be remembered under the new agent
findings.body:
The switch effect (useConversation.ts:216-238) calls `setSkills([])`, but the state only changes on the next render. `ChatSessionScreen.tsx:379-382` runs `rememberChatSkills(host, skillsHarness, projectId, conversation.skills)` in an effect with `skillsHarness` and `conversation.skills` as dependencies. `skillsHarness` comes from `conversation.snapshot?.harness`, which changes in the same commit as the switch. In that commit the screen's effect fires with the new harness (e.g. codex) and the outgoing agent's `conversation.skills` (claude-code), because the hook's `setSkills([])` has not applied yet. That stores claude's list under the codex key. The follow-up render passes `[]`, which `rememberChatSkills` ignores (`!skills.length`). The New task page (`rememberedChatSkills`, used in `spawnSkills.ts:20`) then offers claude's skills for codex until a codex chat reports its own list. That is the cross-agent leak this PR sets out to close. The new test only checks `conversation.skills` and never the remembered list, so it does not catch this. A fix is to remember only skills that were loaded for the harness shown, for example by having the hook expose the harness its `skills` belong to and having the screen pass that to `rememberChatSkills`. I did not run this, so the ordering rests on React's effect and state semantics.

Also: `rememberedSkills.test.ts` does not cover this path.

contracts.action: Switching a chat's agent now clears its skills list and the skills cache entry
contracts.equivalent_path: The models/config-options catalog reset in the same effect (useConversation.ts:230-234), and reloadMcp's skills reset (useConversation.ts:639-640).
contracts.before_after: Before: the outgoing agent's skills stayed in state and in skillsCache (30s TTL). After: both are cleared on a harness change within the same cacheKey. The ChatSessionScreen effect that remembers skills for the New task page still runs once with the stale list under the new harness key.
contracts.visible_effect: The chat's "/" menu is empty after a switch until loadSkills runs again. The New task page can still receive the outgoing agent's list under the new agent.
contracts.failure_mode: The new loadSkills is skipped for stale-harness results (returns [] and drops the cache entry). Errors fall back to `skills`. A deleted pending cache entry is not re-set by the old promise, because the cache checks `entries.get(key) === pending` (asyncValueCache.ts:66).

contracts.action: rememberChatSkills stores a chat's list under its own project key only, with no machine-wide copy
contracts.equivalent_path: loadSpawnSkills in spawnSkills.ts:20, which calls rememberedChatSkills(hostId, agent, projectId).
contracts.before_after: Before: every chat also wrote the machine-wide key, so a project chat's skills reached other projects. After: only a chat with no project writes it, and a project falls back to that or to an empty list.
contracts.visible_effect: The New task page for a project with no chat of its own shows only the list from a no-project chat, or nothing, not another project's skills. Built-in commands such as /compact are missing there until a no-project chat has reported.
contracts.failure_mode: No error path. It is a synchronous in-memory map with a 32-entry LRU.

summary: One finding. The agent-switch reset in useConversation.ts leaves a hole: ChatSessionScreen's remember effect still runs once with the outgoing agent's skills under the new agent's key. The reset only fixes `conversation.skills`, not the remembered list the New task page reads. The rememberedSkills.ts change and the stale-load guard in loadSkills look correct against the cache semantics. The tests are sound for what they assert, but none checks the remembered list after a switch.
